headline: Software Engineer Decides to Code Entirely in Morse Code to Better Align with Company’s ‘Workforce Strategy’
body:
Following the latest corporate announcements regarding workforce distribution and global mobility, senior software architect Rohan Kulkarni has announced his decision to transition his entire daily output into International Morse Code. Kulkarni, who claims he is simply staying ahead of potential geopolitical fluctuations, believes that if his physical presence in international offices is no longer guaranteed, his data should at least be transmitted in a format that feels 'remotely ancient and highly portable.'

“The company mentioned that their workforce strategy remains unfazed by visa changes, and I took that to heart,” said Kulkarni, who spent Tuesday afternoon meticulously tapping out a 4,000-line Java module on a custom-built telegraph key. “If the border authorities ever decide that my code is ‘too digital,’ I want to be able to broadcast the entire sprint backlog from a handheld flashlight or a series of well-placed smoke signals. It’s about building a future-proof stack that transcends international transit hurdles.”

Management has reportedly been supportive of the shift, noting that while the build times have increased by roughly 400%, the lack of human interaction during the translation process has inadvertently reduced office noise pollution. 'We don't need a physical presence in a specific zip code when our team members are essentially operating like deep-space relay stations,' said a project manager who requested to remain anonymous. 'It’s a bold, albeit extremely slow, step toward true borderless infrastructure.'
caption: When the workforce strategy is so robust, you don't even need high-speed internet anymore. The future of coding is just rhythmic clicking. #TechLife #WorkforceStrategy #MorseCode #Innovation (satire)
